svg.text: A Standalone sub-mechanisms — six machine-tool tricks
Each panel loops on its own. These parts can be used in any concept (A1–A4 or others).
source: A-machine-tool.md section 2
M3, M7, M16 are shown in the A2 / A4 drawings
M1 Expansion-mandrel spindle nose
Every tool is a plain part with an H7 bore. Disc springs keep
it clamped on power loss; air blast cleans the bore first.
Grip ≈ 80–150 Nm; no balls, keys or threads face the food.
M5 Slit-and-jet onion skinning
One shallow slit, then a water jet aimed against the spin
gets under the dry skin and unwinds it in 3–5 s
(mains water 4 bar, 2 L/min; no compressor).
M6 Pipe-cutter egg cracking
The egg turns once against a carbide point (0.3 mm score),
then the cups pull apart with a twist. The contents drop;
each cup keeps its half shell for disposal. 8 s per egg.
M9 Freeze gripper ("ice vice")
A −10 °C Peltier platen freezes onto one wet slice
in 5–15 s and lifts exactly one; reversing the current
releases it in 2 s. Also holds fillets flat for cutting.
M10 Dosing by machining
Sticky things are kept as bar stock and shaved off
until the weigh pad says stop: 20 g butter ± 1 g,
no pump, spoon or smeared spout. Same cycle grates cheese.
M17 Flip bracket: pan-to-pan

g.text: the spindle leads the pair through a half circle

svg.text: A second hot pan is set rim-to-rim; the pair turns 180°
about a passive wall pivot. Flips pancake, omelette, Rösti;
unmoulds a cake. Stopped at 100–130° it is a pour bracket.
Each panel loops by itself (6–7 s). Orange = moving mechanism, blue = water, purple = elastomer.
